brief:
Four prominent US human rights organizations have filed suit against the Trump administration, challenging an executive order that imposes sanctions on the International Criminal Court, The Guardian reported. The groups argue the measures are "crippling" and designed to obstruct the court's investigation into alleged Israeli crimes in Palestine. The lawsuit seeks to halt what the organizations characterize as an unlawful attempt to interfere with the ICC's independent work.

The plaintiffs contend that the sanctions violate principles of international law and established procedures for judicial independence. They argue the Trump administration exceeded its constitutional authority by targeting a body investigating matters the US government finds politically inconvenient. The case centers on whether executive power extends to punishing international courts that conduct investigations without US approval.

title: Human rights groups sue Trump over ICC sanctions
